parts.title: Foundations: Machines, Data and the Shape of an Engine
parts.summary: The physics of storage and durability, the data models and SQL a beginner needs, and a map of a database engine including a WAL primer so every later module has its anchors.

parts.title: Storage Engines: Pages, Trees, Logs and Columns
parts.summary: The single-node storage substrate in depth: page layout, buffer management, B-trees and LSM trees, the full family of access methods, practical index selection, and columnar analytical storage.

parts.title: Query Processing: From SQL Text to Executed Plan
parts.summary: Parsing, rewriting, physical operators, cost-based optimization, execution engines with resource control, and the EXPLAIN literacy that ties them together.

parts.title: Transactions, Concurrency Control and Recovery
parts.summary: Serializability and isolation levels precisely, locking, MVCC from semantics through vacuum, non-blocking serializability, and write-ahead logging with ARIES recovery.

parts.title: Using the Database Well
parts.summary: Advanced SQL, application access paths, modeling and per-store usage, application data patterns, and zero-downtime schema evolution on a single database.

parts.title: Distributed Foundations: Failure, Consistency, Time and Truth
parts.summary: Why distribute at all, the consistency model hierarchy, clocks and ordering, and failure detection with leases and fencing — the rules before the protocols.

parts.title: Replication, Partitioning and Consensus
parts.summary: How data is copied, split and agreed upon: leader-based replication, sharding with modeling for partitioned stores, Dynamo-style quorums and CRDTs, then Paxos, Raft and coordination services.

parts.title: Distributed Transactions, Architectures, Streams and Verification
parts.summary: Atomic commit and distributed SQL protocols, cloud-native and disaggregated architectures, distributed and analytical query execution, logs and derived data, and how distributed claims are verified.

parts.title: Real-System Case Studies
parts.summary: One page per engine, tying every mechanism module to how a shipping system actually assembles storage, query, transactions and replication.

parts.title: Production Practice
parts.summary: Securing, operating, tuning, sizing, backing up and recovering databases, plus the incidents that recur and what postmortems teach.

parts.title: Senior Engineer Judgement
parts.summary: Performance literacy, tradeoff reasoning and misconceptions, then capstone designs, toy-engine builds and the hardware frontier.

parts.title: Reference, Playbooks and Decision Guides
parts.summary: The lookup half of the site: a glossary that disambiguates the field's overloaded words, notation and anchor-number cards, theorem-to-consequence rules, engine and managed-platform comparison matrices, symptom-first on-call playbooks, and an annotated reading map. Nothing here introduces a mechanism — every entry states a fact, a rule or a diagnostic and links to the module that derives it, so the site can be entered sideways from a search engine or mid-incident rather than only read front to back.
